newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung Elect up on book-to-bill ratio.
newsitem.headline: Samsung Elect up on book-to-bill ratio.

text.p: Shares in South Korea's largest chipmaker Samsung Electronics rose 2.6 percent in early Wednesday trading on news of a rising book-to-bill ratio, brokers said.
Samsung Electronics gained 1,800 won to 69,300 with 11,130 shares changing hands.
"Samsung Electronics came under the spotlight this morning as the book-to-bill ratio rose in September," said Choi Dong-chul, broker at Ssangyong Securities.

The U.S. Semiconductor Industry Association said on Tuesday the North American book-to-bill ratio, which measures the value of orders against shipments, rose to 0.99 in September from a revised 0.93 in August.
The ratio means manufacturers received $99 in new orders last months for every $100 in shipments.
